cls: Immunomodulator - synthetic random polypeptide (disease-modifying therapy for MS)
pharm: A synthetic mixture of polypeptides that modifies the immune processes thought to underlie multiple sclerosis, reducing relapse frequency; given by subcutaneous injection
quick: 20 mg SC once daily OR 40 mg SC three times weekly (>=48 h apart); strengths not interchangeable
No clear evidence of harm; use if clearly needed (generally considered low risk)
Minimal systemic absorption; considered compatible with breastfeeding by many guidelines
No specific dose adjustment; largely hydrolysed locally
Rare hepatic injury reported; consider stopping if hepatic dysfunction occurs
Injection-site reactions, immediate post-injection reactions, hepatic signs
summary: Glatiramer acetate is a synthetic random polypeptide immunomodulator used as a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease and active secondary progressive disease. It is given by subcutaneous injection only, either 20 mg/mL once daily or 40 mg/mL three times weekly (at least 48 hours apart); the two strengths are NOT interchangeable. Its mechanism is not fully understood but is thought to involve modification of immune processes (induction of glatiramer-specific regulatory T cells). Notable effects include injection-site reactions, lipoatrophy/skin necrosis, and a characteristic transient immediate post-injection reaction (flushing, chest tightness, palpitations, dyspnoea, anxiety) occurring in roughly 16% of patients on the 20 mg dose; transient chest pain may also occur. It is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to glatiramer acetate or mannitol.
indications: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults - clinically isolated syndrome

dosage.t: Subcutaneous injection (arms, abdomen, hips, thighs - rotate sites)
dosage.n: Not interchangeable with the 40 mg product

dosage.d: 40 mg subcutaneously three times per week, at least 48 hours apart
dosage.n: Not interchangeable with the 20 mg product

admin: For subcutaneous use only - do not give intravenously
Remove the prefilled syringe from the refrigerator and let it stand at room temperature for about 20 minutes before injecting
Inspect the solution - it should be clear and colourless to slightly yellow; discard if particulate matter or discoloration is present
Rotate injection sites among arms, abdomen, hips and thighs to reduce lipoatrophy and skin necrosis
Each prefilled syringe is single-use; discard unused portions
Counsel patients that an immediate post-injection reaction (flushing, chest tightness, palpitations) may occur and is usually transient and self-limited
moa: The mechanism by which glatiramer acetate exerts its effect in multiple sclerosis is not fully understood, but it is thought to act by modifying immune processes believed to be responsible for MS pathogenesis. Studies in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis and in vitro systems suggest that on administration glatiramer-specific suppressor/regulatory T cells are induced and activated in the periphery, producing a shift toward anti-inflammatory cytokines and bystander suppression of myelin-directed autoimmunity. Because it can modify immune function, there is a theoretical concern about altering naturally occurring immune responses, though this has not been demonstrated.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to glatiramer acetate or to mannitol
relative: History of severe immediate post-injection reactions
Significant cardiac disease (transient chest pain/palpitations may occur)
Pre-existing hepatic impairment (rare hepatic injury reported)

preg: Available data have not shown a drug-associated increase in major birth defects or miscarriage; glatiramer acetate is generally regarded as relatively low-risk and may be used in pregnancy if clearly needed. Discuss benefits and risks; MS relapse risk during pregnancy should be weighed against any theoretical drug risk.
lact: Glatiramer acetate has minimal systemic absorption and is a large polypeptide unlikely to be appreciably present in or absorbed from breast milk. Many guidelines consider it compatible with breastfeeding; weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is recommended in renal impairment; glatiramer acetate is largely hydrolysed locally to amino acids with negligible systemic/renal handling. Pharmacokinetics in renal impairment have not been formally studied.
hepatic: Rare cases of hepatic injury (including severe liver injury and rare hepatic failure) have been reported. If signs or symptoms of hepatic dysfunction occur, consider discontinuing glatiramer acetate. No routine dose adjustment is specified.

major: No clinically significant drug-drug interactions have been established
moderate: Other immunosuppressive/immunomodulatory therapies - additive immune effects (limited data)
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; rare transaminase elevations may occur

common: Injection-site reactions (erythema, pain, induration, pruritus, swelling)
Immediate post-injection reaction (flushing, chest tightness, palpitations, anxiety, dyspnoea, throat constriction, urticaria) - transient
serious: Lipoatrophy and, rarely, skin necrosis at injection sites
Severe immediate post-injection reactions requiring medical care
Hepatic injury including rare hepatic failure
emergency: Severe or prolonged post-injection reaction with cardiorespiratory symptoms

monitoring: Injection-site appearance for lipoatrophy or skin necrosis
Occurrence and severity of immediate post-injection reactions
Signs and symptoms of hepatic dysfunction (jaundice, dark urine, fatigue)
counsel: Inject just under the skin and rotate sites (arms, tummy, hips, thighs) to avoid dents or damage to the skin
Let the syringe warm to room temperature (about 20 minutes) before injecting to reduce discomfort
Soon after an injection you may briefly feel flushing, chest tightness, a fast heartbeat or shortness of breath - this usually passes within minutes; seek help if it is severe or lasts
Do not inject if the liquid is cloudy or has particles
Report yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine or persistent tiredness, which could signal a liver problem
Keep the syringes refrigerated; they may be kept at room temperature for up to a month if needed, but do not freeze
pk: Immunomodulatory effect develops gradually over weeks to months
Locally hydrolysed at the injection site; little intact drug reaches the circulation
Not meaningfully defined - rapidly degraded to amino acids/peptides at the injection site
Sustained disease-modifying effect with ongoing regular dosing
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; may be kept at 15-30 C for up to one month; do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: 20 mg/mL daily and 40 mg/mL three-times-weekly products are NOT interchangeable
Characteristic immediate post-injection reaction (flushing, chest tightness, palpitations) affects ~16% on 20 mg - transient and self-limited, but reassure and recognise
Rotate injection sites to limit lipoatrophy and skin necrosis
Considered one of the lower-risk MS DMTs in pregnancy and lactation
Note for openFDA: indexed under brand labels (e.g. Glatopa/Copaxone) - use the glatiramer acetate prescribing information
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that day; if it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed one and resume your regular schedule. For the three-times-weekly product keep doses at least 48 hours apart. Do not double up.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Monitor and treat supportively. Watch for and manage hypersensitivity/post-injection reactions; there is no specific antidote.
